## 1. What uv is — 0:00 to 0:31

[Scene 1. The claim, a card for what it replaces, a card for how it is built, then the promise.]

uv is one program that replaces a whole shelf of Python tools. [beat] It installs packages, it
builds virtual environments, it resolves a lockfile, and it installs Python itself. [beat] It is
written in Rust, and it keeps one cache for your whole machine, so a wheel you have already
downloaded is linked into a new project rather than fetched twice. [beat] That is why a cold
install finishes in seconds.
takes.text:
uv is one program that replaces a whole shelf of Python tools. —

It installs packages, it builds virtual environments, it resolves a lockfile, and it installs Python itself. —

It is written in Rust, and it keeps one cache for your whole machine, so a wheel you have already downloaded is linked into a new project rather than fetched twice. —

That is why a cold install finishes in seconds.

[Scene 2. Opens on scene 1's last picture, gives way to its own on the handoff, then the heading, the unix command, the windows command, and the update line.]

Before any of that, uv has to be on your machine. [beat]
Install it with the standalone installer, which needs no Python on the machine first. [beat] On
macOS and Linux, pipe the script from astral dot sh into your shell. [beat] On Windows, run the
same script through powershell. [beat] Homebrew and pip ex both carry uv as well, and either one is

Before any of that, uv has to be on your machine. —

Install it with the standalone installer, which needs no Python on the machine first. —

## 3. Start a project — 1:05 to 1:40

[Scene 3. Opens on scene 2's last picture, gives way to its own on the handoff, then the heading, the files init writes, and the two cards about what has not happened yet.]

With uv installed, the next step is a project. [beat]
Run uv init and give your project a name. [beat] uv writes four files: a pyproject dot tommel that
declares the project, a read me, a starter module, and a dot python dash version file that pins the
interpreter this project wants. [beat] Nothing is installed yet, and there is no virtual
environment yet either. [beat] uv builds one for you the first time you ask it to run something.

## 4. Add and remove dependencies — 1:40 to 2:18

[Scene 4. Opens on scene 3's last picture, gives way to its own on the handoff, then the heading, the card for the one step, the dev dependency card, and the remove line.]

An empty project needs packages, so add your first one. [beat]
uv add httpx is how a package joins your project. [beat] It resolves the dependency, writes it into
pyproject dot tommel, updates the lockfile, and installs it into the environment, all in one step.
[beat] For a package you need only while developing, name the group, so uv add dash dash group dev
pytest records pytest under the dependency groups table. [beat] uv remove takes a
package back out, and the lockfile and the environment both follow it.
takes.text:
An empty project needs packages, so add your first one. —

uv add httpx is how a package joins your project. —

It resolves the dependency, writes it into pyproject dot tommel, updates the lockfile, and installs it into the environment, all in one step. —

For a package you need only while developing, name the group, so uv add dash dash group dev pytest records pytest under the dependency groups table. —

uv remove takes a package back out, and the lockfile and the environment both follow it.

takes.markdown:
## 5. Lock and sync — 2:18 to 2:53

[Scene 5. Opens on scene 4's last picture, gives way to its own on the handoff, then the heading, the sync line, a card for committing and a card for continuous integration.]

Every one of those steps touched the lockfile. [beat]
uv lock writes a lockfile that pins every package, for every platform your project claims to
support. [beat] uv sync then makes your environment match that lockfile exactly, installing what is
missing and removing whatever does not belong. [beat] Commit the lockfile, because it is what makes
the install reproducible for everybody else. [beat] In continuous integration, pass the frozen flag,
so uv installs straight from the lockfile and never resolves it again.
takes.text:
Every one of those steps touched the lockfile. —

uv lock writes a lockfile that pins every package, for every platform your project claims to support. —

uv sync then makes your environment match that lockfile exactly, installing what is missing and removing whatever does not belong. —

Commit the lockfile, because it is what makes the install reproducible for everybody else. —

In continuous integration, pass the frozen flag, so uv installs straight from the lockfile and never resolves it again.

takes.markdown:
## 6. Run tools and scripts — 2:53 to 3:32

[Scene 6. Opens on scene 5's last picture, gives way to its own on the handoff, then the heading, the two tool commands, and the single file script.]

With everything in sync, it is time to run something. [beat]
uv run runs a command inside your project's environment, and it syncs before it starts, so what
runs is always what the lockfile says. [beat] uvx runs a tool once without installing it anywhere
at all. [beat] uv tool install keeps a tool on your path for good. [beat] And a single file script
can declare its own dependencies in a comment header at the top, so running it builds an
environment just for that file and throws it away afterwards.
takes.text:
With everything in sync, it is time to run something. —

uv run runs a command inside your project's environment, and it syncs before it starts, so what runs is always what the lockfile says. —

uvx runs a tool once without installing it anywhere at all. —

uv tool install keeps a tool on your path for good. —

And a single file script can declare its own dependencies in a comment header at the top, so running it builds an environment just for that file and throws it away afterwards.

takes.markdown:
## 7. The whole workflow — 3:32 to 3:53

[Scene 7. Opens on scene 6's last picture, gives way to the recap card, then one row for each of the five commands, each on its own words.]

So that is uv, and your project fits on one card. [beat]
uv init starts it, uv add grows it, uv lock pins it, uv sync matches it, and uv run uses it. [beat]
That's the whole workflow, in one tool.
